name: Channel-mode (broadcast vs precise) common-mode null
estimator: identical to step_2_0: timestamp intersection, linear detrend, Welch MSC 10-500 uHz

shared_power_ns2.note: band-integrated Re(cross-spectrum): unbiased shared variance (ns^2); independent noise contributes zero in expectation, so channel amplitudes are directly comparable despite the precise channel's higher per-series noise

commonmode_template_projection.note: projection of the measured common-mode template onto the broadcast channel's shared-power profile: a_cm is the common-mode-shaped contribution admitted by the data

carrier_validation_vs_fcv.note: D-channel shared power should track the measured common-view fraction if D carries the satellite carrier; the broadcast signal is shown for contrast

interpretation: The difference series D = broadcast − precise contains every element of the broadcast SPP solve absent from the precise-product solve — the satellite clock/orbit common mode plus inter-solve modelling differences — so its distance-structured coherence is a strict upper envelope on what the broadcast common-mode carrier can supply.  The precise channel retains the broadcast-free signal.
verdict: Channel-mode decomposition on 22707 real pair-days measures the broadcast satellite-product common mode directly and excludes it as the driver on three legs.  (1) The carrier is real and at the expected scale: the broadcast-minus-precise difference channel carries 470 ns^2 of distance-structured shared power at lambda = 5207 km — the constellation-footprint scale (and its binned profile tracks the Step 2.10 common-view fraction, Spearman rho = 0.74) — versus the measured signal's lambda = 843 km (MSC) / 2230 km (shared power).  (2) The broadcast-free channel retains the signal: the precise-products solve, into which broadcast satellite clock (~1-5 ns) and orbit (~1-5 m) errors cannot enter at all, keeps a distance-structured excess of 373 ns^2 shared power (MSC amplitude 0.105 at lambda = 1922 km) — comparable to or exceeding the broadcast channel's entire 164 ns^2 excess.  (3) Projecting the measured common-mode template onto the broadcast shared-power profile admits at most ~54% common-mode-shaped content (an upper bound — the difference channel is a superset of the carrier and the two decay profiles are partially degenerate), leaving 111 ns^2 of residual structure at lambda = 660 km the carrier cannot supply.
